cells.tense: You are walking toward a light you picked, and the picking feels like yours.
cells.ask: Say the direction to one person in one sentence, then take the step that sentence asks for before the week ends.
cells.core:
You are moving with a light in front of you, and you chose it. The road is not mapped and that is all right — you do not need the whole thing, only the next stretch. What you are pointed at already holds your attention, which is why you can walk without demanding certainty from the ground. Direction here is a picture you keep returning to, not a plan you force.

And this is not something you keep by holding still. It stays because you keep feeding it — the pull gets followed rather than audited. Someone near you can help carry it. That is how a solo picture stays from turning brittle. When you say out loud where you are going, the direction gets firmer, not smaller.
cells.sheetLine: You chose the light, so keep walking toward it.
cells.verb: Pull a direction out of the picture and light one step of it.
cells.place: In half-light on an unfinished road, where one step shows and the rest does not.

cells.tense: You are trying to force a whole route out of a picture that only shows one turn.
cells.ask: Take the fork that scares you least and commit to it for three days, then stop and look at what the walking taught you.
cells.core:
You are acting like the fog has to clear before you can move, and the clearing is eating the moving. Each option gets examined for the one that will not embarrass you later, so the road stays in pieces and no foot goes down. The push for certainty is louder than the pull that got you started.

Not seeing the whole route is the condition you are walking in, not a problem to solve before you begin. Let the next step come from the picture rather than from a guarantee about the end of it. Commit to something small and see what the world says back. Direction does not get safer by being studied; it gets usable by being walked.

cells.tense: You stopped walking toward the light and your feet have stayed where they were.
cells.ask: Write the direction that still pulls you at the top of a page, and read it out loud before your day starts.
cells.core:
The light is still in front of you, but the walking toward it has stopped, and the trusting of your own eyes has gone quiet with it. Every option reads as a trap or as a whole life you cannot afford to choose, so you stay where the ground last felt sure.

You do not have to name the whole road or know it is the right one. You need one step that keeps you honest with what you already want. Small tending counts — a sentence you say to yourself, a decision you give a week before judging it. The picture gets clearer from inside the walking, not from the edge of it.

cells.tense: You are already steering by a light, but you describe the course as something that happened to you.
cells.ask: Say one sentence starting with 'I chose this' about a direction you are already walking, and let it stand.
cells.core:
You are moving in a direction — people can see it, and your weeks are organized around it — but you describe it as though it arrived on its own. The steering already happened, quietly, in a place you may not have been watching. What has not happened is owning it out loud, even to yourself.

That is not a dramatic failure. It is closer to a hand that did the work and did not get named. The point is not to announce a mission; it is to bring the steering back where you can adjust it. When you say the direction is yours, you can turn it. Someone holding the other end of it can help. They cannot hold a thing you will not claim.

attempts.check: The record supports Direction as the card's capacity, ambiguity as the seat, and the four mechanisms, but it never says what a person has already chosen or what past room they are avoiding, so the Too Little and Unacknowledged cells must narrow to the mechanism rather than supply a history. A reader could reasonably object that a card about choosing a star isn't about uncertainty or imagination at all, so every cell has to keep both the pulling light and the partial view in play. The asks survive a wrong read because each is one visible act — writing a list, drawing the route, telling someone what pulls — that teaches the person something about their own deciding even if the map missed. The sentence that serves me more than the person is any line suggesting the direction was always there and waiting to be noticed, which flatters a Reader rather than handing over a next move.
